verdict.rationale: Slate's docs describe orchestrating multiple subagents in parallel, showing them as a grid of cards and allowing users to 'spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once,' which supports bulk-style operations across many items/tasks. However, there's no explicit example of true bulk operations (e.g., batch file edits, mass refactors) and no independent/hands-on evidence corroborating this orchestration works well at scale — community commentary raises skepticism about output quality on a related porting task. Missing for 10: concrete bulk-operation examples (e.g., editing/processing many files/items in one command), and independent verification that parallel orchestration scales reliably.
